# Glow and Sculpt Facial

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/glow-and-sculpt-facial-chattanooga.html

Glow and Sculpt Facial

# Dermaplane, Hydrate, *Sculpt*

A 45-minute facial that pairs the immediate smoothness of dermaplaning with the lift and relaxation of cool jade comb sculpting. A hydrating jelly mask in the middle. A heated neck pillow throughout..

[Book Glow & Sculpt](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)
[See the Experience](#the-experience)

## The Service, in Their Words

"This 45-minute experience begins with gentle dermaplaning to exfoliate and reveal a smoother, more radiant complexion. Next, a hydrating jelly mask is applied while you unwind with a heated neck pillow, melting away tension. To finish, cool jade combs are used to massage and sculpt the face, promoting circulation and a natural lift. Leave feeling smooth, glowing, and deeply relaxed."

## Why This Combination Works

Most facials do one thing well. The Glow and Sculpt does three things, in a sequence designed to compound: **exfoliate, hydrate, sculpt**. Each step prepares the skin for the next, and each delivers a distinct visible benefit by the time you leave the room.

### Step 1: Gentle dermaplaning

Your esthetician uses a sterile blade to gently remove the topmost layer of dead skin cells and the fine peach fuzz that traps light and product. This is what produces the immediate smooth-to-the-touch feeling. It also primes the skin so the jelly mask and any finishing serum penetrate more evenly.

If you've never had dermaplaning, you might be expecting something invasive. It's not. The blade glides across taut skin at a precise shallow angle. You'll feel almost nothing — a gentle tickling sensation more than anything else. [More on dermaplaning here.](what-is-dermaplaning.html)

### Step 2: Hydrating jelly mask + heated neck pillow

While the dermaplaning prep settles, your esthetician applies a hydrating jelly mask — a soft, cool gel that delivers concentrated hydration to skin that's just had its protective dead-cell layer removed. The jelly stays on for several minutes, slowly absorbing into the skin.

This is where the heated neck pillow comes in. Warm support under the back of your neck releases the chronic tension most of us carry there from desk work and phone use. You'll feel your shoulders drop. Many guests report this is the moment they actually stop thinking about their day.

### Step 3: Cool jade comb sculpting

Your esthetician finishes the session with cool jade combs — small ridged stone tools used to massage and sculpt the face along specific drainage lines. The technique draws from gua sha (Traditional Chinese Medicine) but uses a more focused tool shape designed for short, targeted lift movements.

Cool jade does several things at once: it temporarily constricts surface blood vessels, which reduces visible puffiness; it stimulates lymphatic flow, which clears the day's accumulated fluid; and the mechanical work releases tension in the small muscles of the face. The visible effect is a sculpted, lifted, awake-looking face within minutes.

### The temperature contrast is the secret

The combination of warm dermaplaning, room-temperature jelly mask, and cool jade combs creates a temperature-contrast experience that's unusually soothing. Many guests describe this as the most genuinely relaxing facial we offer — without sacrificing any of the visible-results work.

## Who This Facial Is Best For

- **Anyone who wants visible lift without injectables.** The jade sculpting produces real, immediate definition in the cheekbones and jawline. It's temporary — days, not months — but it's real.
- **Stressed people.** The heated neck pillow and jade comb sequence is the most directly relaxing facial on our menu.
- **Anyone with puffiness.** Travel, alcohol, poor sleep, allergies, hormonal cycles — jade sculpting addresses fluid retention better than almost anything else we do.
- **Pre-event glow.** 5–7 days before a big event for the smoothness from dermaplaning; the day before for the maximum sculpting effect.
- **Curious about gua sha but unsure about doing it yourself.** Many guests learn from the session and start incorporating gentle home tools into their routine afterward.
- **First-time spa visitors.** Lower commitment than a 60- or 90-minute facial, but more substantive than our 30-minute Express. A great way to try us out.

### When to choose something else instead

- **Active acne or breakouts** — the dermaplaning component is contraindicated. Our [Acne Facial](acne-facial-chattanooga.html) is the right choice.
- **You want the deepest hydration possible** — the [Intraceuticals Oxygen Glow Facial](what-is-an-oxygen-facial.html) delivers more concentrated hyaluronic acid.
- **You want maximum lower-face lift** — consider the standalone 2-hour [Buccal Facial Massage](best-buccal-massage-chattanooga.html).
- **You want deeper resurfacing** — [microdermabrasion](microderm-facial-chattanooga.html) is more aggressive on texture and pores.

[Book Glow & Sculpt](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)

## What to Expect

### Plan to arrive about 5 minutes early

We're by appointment only, so plan to arrive 5 minutes early. We'll text you when it's time to come inside. You'll be greeted with your choice of soothing tea or cold water, settled in a robe, and walked back to a private treatment room.

### The 45 minutes

Cleansing prep, then dermaplaning (10–12 minutes), then jelly mask application with the heated neck pillow in place (10–12 minutes), then jade comb sculpting (15–18 minutes), then finishing serum and SPF.

### What you'll see in the mirror

Smoother skin from the dermaplaning. Plumper, more even-toned skin from the hydration. Reduced puffiness and a more sculpted look from the jade work. Most guests immediately compare before-and-after.

### What you'll feel

Tension you didn't realize you were holding will be gone from your shoulders and jaw. The cool-jade-on-warm-cheeks sensation lingers pleasantly. You'll move slower for the rest of the day.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What's the difference between jade comb sculpting and gua sha?**

Same broad tradition, slightly different tools and intent. Both come from Traditional Chinese Medicine and use cool stone tools to massage and stimulate the face. Gua sha uses a flat-edge stone (often jade, rose quartz, or bian stone) with longer scraping strokes. Jade combs are typically smaller, with multiple ridges, designed for shorter targeted lift movements. The effects are similar — improved circulation, lymphatic drainage, and a sculpted appearance — and many practitioners use both.

**Q: Why are the jade combs cool?**

Cool jade constricts surface blood vessels temporarily, reduces puffiness, and feels deeply soothing on freshly dermaplaned skin. The temperature contrast with the warm dermaplaning and heated neck pillow is part of what makes this facial so distinctively relaxing.

**Q: How is this different from a regular dermaplane facial?**

Both start with dermaplaning. The Dermaplane Facial then focuses on traditional massage, masks, and product layering. The Glow and Sculpt swaps in the jade comb sculpting massage and a jelly mask phase, with a heated neck pillow component. It's the same dermaplaning foundation with a different second half — more focused on lift and sculpting than on layered product work.

**Q: How long do the sculpting effects last?**

Visible lift and reduced puffiness typically last 3–7 days from a single session. The dermaplaning component's smoothness lasts about 3 weeks. With monthly sessions, the cumulative effect compounds — many regulars report their face just looks "set" more often.

**Q: Can I do this during pregnancy?**

Yes — both dermaplaning and jade sculpting are pregnancy-safe. Let your esthetician know so she can choose appropriate finishing products (avoiding retinol or salicylic acid).

**Q: Will my skin be sensitive afterward?**

Possibly briefly. Freshly dermaplaned skin is slightly more sun-sensitive for 2–3 days; SPF is essential. The jade sculpting and jelly mask are non-irritating. No acid exfoliation, no extractions, no heat.

# Therapeutic Massage

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/deep-tissue-massage-chattanooga.html

Deep Tissue Massage

# Real Bodywork. No *Kneading-In-Disguise.*

Licensed massage therapists, sustained pressure, and therapeutic intent. For chronic tension, postural strain, athletic recovery, and the months-old shoulder you've been ignoring.

[Book Massage](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=6)
[Meet the Therapists](https://amberandsagespa.com/#team)

## What "Deep Tissue" Means at Amber & Sage

The label gets abused. A lot of spas slap "deep tissue" on the menu and deliver a slightly firmer Swedish massage with no actual technique. That's not what we do.

Our deep tissue massage is genuine therapeutic bodywork — sustained pressure into specific muscle layers and fascial planes, with the goal of changing tissue, not just temporarily quieting it. Our therapists are licensed, trained in multiple modalities, and most have specialized continuing education in injury rehab, sports massage, or manual fascial therapy.

### Who books deep tissue here

The Chattanooga crowd skews active. We see a lot of:

- **Runners** on the Riverwalk — tight calves, IT bands, plantar fascia, hip flexors.
- **Cyclists** training on Suck Creek, Raccoon Mountain, and the Cherokee section — locked-up traps, neck rotators, quads.
- **Climbers** from the Tennessee Bouldering Authority and surrounding areas — forearms, lats, rhomboids, finger pulleys.
- **Desk-bound knowledge workers** — thoracic, suboccipital, levator scapulae, the whole upper-cross postural pattern.
- **Parents of young kids** — lower back, glutes, neck, the constant-carry shoulders.
- **Post-PT clients** who graduated from physical therapy and want maintenance massage to keep gains.

### Tell us what's actually going on

Walk in with a complaint, not a service name. "My right SI joint has been off since the half marathon" is more useful than "I want deep tissue." Your therapist will pick technique accordingly — which might mean cupping, Graston, myofascial stretch, or actual deep tissue, often in combination.

### Modalities we combine with deep tissue

- **Cupping therapy** — negative-pressure suction for fascial decompression. Leaves the famous round marks; they're not bruises.
- **Graston technique** — instrument-assisted soft tissue work for stubborn adhesions and scar tissue.
- **Myofascial stretch therapy** — assisted stretching to restore range of motion.
- **Hot stone** — heated basalt stones to warm tissue before deep work. Surprisingly useful with chronic tension.
- **Aromatherapy** — essential-oil pairing to deepen your session.

### What a 90-minute deep tissue session looks like

Five minutes of consultation. You tell us where it hurts, what aggravates it, what you've tried. Your therapist will likely do some standing assessment — range-of-motion checks, palpation of the suspect tissue. From there: heat or warming techniques to prep the tissue, broad strokes to map and warm the body, then specific work into the targeted areas. We'll dose pressure based on continuous feedback. The last 10 minutes are usually integration — gentler strokes to let the nervous system settle. You'll get aftercare notes (hydrate, walk, avoid heavy lifting for 24 hours).

## Massage Modalities on Our Menu

### Deep Tissue

Sustained pressure, specific layers. Our most-requested service.

### Swedish

Long flowing strokes for relaxation and circulation. Excellent first-time-here choice.

### East Asian Style

A relaxing blend of Thai, Chinese, and Japanese techniques paired with trigger point therapy to release deep tension and restore balance. 60 or 90 minutes.

### Prenatal

Side-lying with bolsters, gentle pressure, trained therapists. Safe and welcomed in any trimester (with clearance).

### Hot Stone

Heated basalt stones warm tissue and allow deeper work without higher pressure.

### Cupping

Negative-pressure suction cups. Often combined with deep tissue.

### Couples

Side-by-side rooms. Great for anniversaries or shared birthdays.

### [Body Scrub](body-scrub-chattanooga.html)

[Book Massage](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=6)

## Massage FAQ

**Q: What's the difference between deep tissue and Swedish massage?**

Swedish massage uses long, flowing strokes for general relaxation. Deep tissue applies sustained pressure to specific layers of muscle and fascia, addressing chronic tension and adhesions. Both are valid — most clients alternate or combine depending on what they need.

**Q: Is deep tissue massage supposed to hurt?**

It can feel intense but should never be painful in a "flinch" sense. Communicate with your therapist throughout — we adjust pressure constantly based on your feedback. The goal is therapeutic, not punishing.

**Q: How long should my session be?**

60 minutes is enough for one to two focused areas. For full-body deep work, 90 minutes is the sweet spot. Two hours is available and excellent if you have multiple concerns or want to combine modalities like cupping.

**Q: Do you do sports or injury-rehab massage?**

Yes. Several of our therapists specialize in sports massage, cupping, Graston technique, and myofascial release for athletes, runners, climbers, and post-PT clients.

**Q: Can I get a deep tissue massage during pregnancy?**

We don't recommend deep tissue specifically during pregnancy, but we offer prenatal massage from therapists trained in side-lying positioning and pregnancy-safe technique. Book under "prenatal" rather than "deep tissue."

**Q: How often should I get a massage?**

Depends on your goal. For chronic-tension management, every 2–4 weeks is common. For event-driven recovery (race, big project, surgery follow-up), targeted sessions work. Athletes in training often get weekly sessions.

# Seasonal Body Scrub

Seasonal Body Scrub

# Soft, Smooth, *Restored*

A 30-minute full-body exfoliation with Éminence's all-natural Coconut Sugar Scrub. Standalone, or as an enhancement to a massage or facial. The kind of treatment you walk out of feeling like a new person.

[Book a Body Scrub](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=6)
[What's In It](#what-it-does)

## The Service, in Their Words

"This luxurious full-body exfoliation uses Éminence's all-natural Coconut Sugar Scrub to gently buff away dead skin cells, leaving your skin silky smooth and deeply hydrated. The organic coconut oil nourishes and softens, while raw sugar polishes and revitalizes. The treatment begins with a warm application of the scrub, followed by soothing circular massage strokes to improve circulation. After a refreshing shower, your skin is left glowing, smooth, and delicately scented with tropical coconut. Perfect as a standalone refresh or added after a massage or before a facial."

## What's Actually Happening

Body scrubs sound simple — sugar plus oil, rubbed onto skin. The difference between a forgettable scrub and a transformative one is in the ingredients, the technique, and the integration with the rest of the visit.

### The product: Éminence Coconut Sugar Scrub

We use Éminence's organic Coconut Sugar Scrub — the same biodynamic brand we partner with for all our facial work. Raw sugar provides the gentle mechanical exfoliation; organic coconut oil delivers hydration and softness; tropical coconut scent leaves you faintly fragrant for hours. No synthetic fragrances, no harsh exfoliants, no plastic microbeads (banned in cosmetics for good reason).

### The technique

Your therapist begins by warming the scrub before application — cold sugar on warm skin is uncomfortable; warm scrub feels like a coastal moment. The scrub is applied in sections (legs first, then arms, back, torso) and worked in with slow, soothing circular massage strokes that double as gentle lymphatic stimulation. The combination of exfoliation, massage, and oil absorption is what produces the visible glow.

### The shower

After the scrub work is complete, you'll move to our shower to rinse. The sugar dissolves easily; the coconut oil leaves a light, nourishing film on the skin that doesn't need to be washed off aggressively. This is the moment most clients say feels best — warm water on freshly exfoliated, oil-conditioned skin.

### What you'll notice

Immediately: skin is dramatically smoother to the touch. For 2–3 days afterward: lotion absorbs deeper and faster; everything feels softer; the faint coconut scent lingers; clothing slides on differently. For 5–7 days: the smoothness gradually settles back, but the skin holds moisturizer better than it did before the scrub.

### Why "seasonal"?

We rotate our scrub menu through the year — coconut sugar is our current default, but seasonal variations may appear as the calendar shifts. The structure and benefits are consistent; the scent profile evolves with the seasons.

## Standalone or as an Enhancement

The body scrub is one of our most flexible services because it works equally well on its own or layered into a longer visit.

### As a standalone

30 minutes of focused full-body exfoliation. Perfect as a quick mid-week refresh, a beach-trip prep, a "between-massages" maintenance visit, or a "I just need to feel like a person again" decompression.

### After a massage

The most-popular pairing. Get a 60- or 90-minute [therapeutic massage](deep-tissue-massage-chattanooga.html) first, then a body scrub afterward. The scrub removes the massage oil, the post-scrub shower leaves you completely fresh, and you walk out the door feeling like you just had a half-day at a destination spa. Add 30 minutes to your massage booking and ask for the scrub to follow.

### Before a facial

Less common but excellent for a "full-day reset" visit. Body scrub first, then move to a facial — [which facial to choose](which-facial-should-i-get.html) is a separate question, but Personalized Éminence and Glow and Sculpt both pair beautifully here.

### Wedding-week prep

3–5 days before the wedding, book a body scrub. Your skin will be at its smoothest for the dress fitting, the dress itself, and the honeymoon afterward. Pair with lash and brow services in the same visit and you've handled most of your bridal prep in a single appointment.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What does the body scrub actually do?**

It mechanically exfoliates the entire body — sloughing off dead skin cells from your back, shoulders, arms, legs, and torso using fine raw sugar suspended in nourishing oils. The exfoliation is followed by soothing massage strokes, then a warm shower. The result is skin that's noticeably smoother and softer, and that holds moisturizer and lotion dramatically better for days afterward.

**Q: Will the scrub be too rough on sensitive skin?**

No — the sugar granules in Éminence's Coconut Sugar Scrub are fine and naturally dissolve as they're worked into the skin. The oils make the texture creamy rather than gritty. It's gentler than most salt-based scrubs and far gentler than mechanical body brushing.

**Q: Do I need to bring anything?**

No. We provide robes, towels, and everything you'll need for the post-scrub shower. Just come clothed — you'll change in a private treatment room, and you'll have full draping throughout the service.

**Q: Should I shave or wax beforehand?**

Avoid shaving or waxing the same day — freshly exfoliated skin is more sensitive to the sugar. Two to three days before is ideal if you want smooth, hair-free skin going into your scrub appointment.

**Q: Should I get a body scrub before or after a massage?**

After is typically better. A massage often uses oil that you'd then want to rinse off; doing the scrub afterward removes the oil residue while adding its own nourishing layer. Then the post-scrub shower leaves you feeling completely refreshed at the end of the visit.

**Q: Is this safe during pregnancy?**

Yes — sugar scrubs are generally pregnancy-safe. We use side-lying positioning instead of lying flat on the stomach if you're in your second or third trimester, and we'll skip any areas you're sensitive about. Tell us when you book.

**Q: How often should I get a body scrub?**

Once a month is the most common cadence for regulars. For acute needs (pre-vacation, pre-wedding, between seasons), one-off bookings work well. There's no compounding "series" benefit the way there is with facials — each scrub is a standalone reset.

**Q: What if I'm allergic to coconut?**

Tell us when you book — we may have alternative scrubs available depending on the season, or we may recommend skipping the service. Coconut allergies are rare but real, and we won't risk a reaction.

# Lash & Brow Services

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/lash-and-brow-chattanooga.html

Lash & Brow in Chattanooga

# Wake Up *Polished*

Lash lifts, brow lamination, and tinting at Amber & Sage. Semi-permanent treatments that mean less makeup, more time, and a face that looks finished from the moment you wake up — for weeks.

[Book Lash & Brow](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=5)
[See the Menu](#menu)

## The "I Can Go Makeup-Free for Weeks" Treatments

The truth about lash and brow services is that almost nobody books them because they want one thing — they book them because they want to *stop* doing something. Stop curling lashes every morning. Stop filling in brows with five different products. Stop reaching for mascara when running out the door.

That's what these treatments do. A lash lift curls your natural lashes for 6–8 weeks. Brow lamination smooths and sets your brow hairs into a defined, fluffy shape for 4–6 weeks. Tinting adds color that lasts as long as the structural treatments. Stack them together and you've effectively swapped 5–10 minutes of morning makeup for a single 90-minute appointment every couple of months.

For brides, that's why these services are some of our most-booked in the weeks leading up to a wedding. For everyone else, it's why they become a habit.

### One review captures it

"I got the Éminence Enzyme facial, brow lamination, lash lift and brow and lash tint — I can go makeup free for weeks!" That's a real client review of stacking the full lash-and-brow combo with a facial. The compounding effect is meaningful.

## Our Lash & Brow Menu

Six services, designed to be mixed and matched.

### Lash Tint


A semi-permanent dye applied to your natural lashes, making them appear darker, fuller, and more defined — the "you, but with mascara on" effect, without the mascara. Particularly transformative for clients with naturally light lashes.

15–20 minutes &middot; Results last 4–6 weeks

### Brow Tint


Semi-permanent dye that fills in sparse areas and defines your natural brow shape. Color stains both the hairs and the skin beneath, so even thin brows look fuller and more shaped immediately.

10–15 minutes &middot; Results last 1–2 weeks on skin, 3–4 weeks on hairs

### Lash and Brow Tint


Both tints in one visit. Coordinated color, less time on the table, a small savings vs. booking separately. Our most-booked tint service.

A semi-permanent curl and lift treatment for your natural lashes. No extensions, no glue, no daily curling. Eyes look more open and awake; lashes appear longer because they're now visible at their full length instead of pointing downward.

45–60 minutes &middot; Results last 6–8 weeks

### Brow Lamination


A chemical treatment that smooths and sets your brow hairs in a fluffy, lifted, defined shape — the "soap brow" look without daily styling. Especially transformative for thin, unruly, or downward-pointing brows.

75–90 minutes &middot; Results last 6–8 weeks

[Book Lash & Brow](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=5)

## What Each Treatment Actually Does

### Lash lift, in plain terms

Your natural eyelashes grow at slightly varying angles — some up, some forward, some downward. A lash lift uses a gentle chemical solution to soften the lashes' protein bonds, then a silicone shield curls them upward in one direction. The bonds re-set in the new curled shape over 6–8 weeks as your lashes naturally shed and regrow.

The result: your eyes look more open, your lashes look longer (because they're now visible at full length rather than pointing forward), and you get the "I curled them" effect without doing it daily. Most clients find they need less mascara, and many skip it entirely while the lift is fresh.

### Brow lamination, in plain terms

Brow lamination uses a similar chemistry to a lash lift but applied to your brow hairs. The hairs are softened, brushed upward into a uniform direction, and then set in that lifted position. The "fluffy brow" look you've seen on Instagram for the last few years — that's brow lamination.

It's transformative for thin or sparse brows because it makes existing hairs look more abundant by spreading them across the brow shape. For unruly brows that go in 50 directions, it tames them into one. For downward-pointing brows that age the face, it creates immediate lift.

### Tints, in plain terms

Tinting is a semi-permanent dye applied to lashes or brows. Different from hair dye in that it's specifically formulated for the eye area and uses much milder developer. The color stains the hairs (and lightly stains the skin underneath for brows), creating immediate visible darkness and definition. The hair color fades gradually over weeks as the hairs shed and regrow; the skin staining on brows fades within a couple of weeks.

### Why people stack them

Lash lift + brow lamination address structure (curl, direction, shape). Tinting adds color. Together they produce the "did you have something done?" look that lasts weeks. Stack with a [facial](eminence-organic-facials-chattanooga.html) in the same visit and you've done the equivalent of a pre-event prep package in 90 minutes.

## Who Books These

### People prepping for events

Weddings (both brides and guests), graduations, reunions, photoshoots, big work events. The combination of lash lift + brow lamination + tinting before an event means you look done in every photo — including the candid ones.

### People who hate doing makeup

If your morning routine takes 20 minutes and you'd love it to take 3, these are the treatments that move the needle. You'll still want a tinted moisturizer and SPF, but the eye-area work is done.

### People with light or sparse lashes/brows

Naturally blonde, gray, or otherwise light lash and brow hair becomes much more visible with tinting alone. Adding lift and lamination amplifies the effect.

### Pre-vacation or pre-honeymoon

Beach trips are the perfect use case. You don't want to worry about mascara running in the ocean or brows smudging in humidity. Lash lifted and laminated brows wake up looking ready every morning of the trip.

### Anyone with downward-pointing lashes

Some people have lashes that just point forward instead of curling up. A lash lift visibly changes the entire shape of the eye area for them — one of the most dramatic before/afters we do.

### Mature clients dealing with brow thinning

Brow hair thins with age. Lamination spreads existing hairs to cover more of the brow shape, and tinting darkens them for definition. Both together are an alternative to microblading for clients who want the look without the long-term commitment.

## What to Know Before You Book

### Avoid water on the area for 24 hours after lift or lamination

No swimming, no steam, no crying jags. The chemistry needs to fully set. After 24 hours, normal showering and washing is fine.

### No oil-based cleansers or makeup removers

For the duration of your lift or lamination, oil-based products break down the chemical bonds and shorten how long results last. Switch to a water-based cleanser; your esthetician will recommend specifics.

### Mascara is fine — after 24–48 hours

Once the lift is set, you can mascara normally. Most clients find they need much less. Some skip it entirely.

### Patch test if you've never had tinting before

Some people are sensitive to tint chemistry. If it's your first time, we may do a small patch test 24–48 hours before your appointment, especially if you have sensitivities to other dyes.

### Sleep face-up the first night if possible

Lashes pressed against a pillow for 8 hours can lose some of their curl. One night of back-sleeping makes a real difference in how long your results stay crisp.

### Book ahead for wedding prep

2–3 weeks before the wedding is the sweet spot for lash lift and brow lamination. Long enough for any settling, close enough that results are at their peak. Tinting is best 5–7 days before the event.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: How long does a lash lift last?**

Typically 6–8 weeks. Your natural lashes shed and regrow on that cycle, so the lift gradually grows out rather than fading. Many clients re-book at the 6-week mark to stay continuously lifted.

**Q: Does a lash lift damage my lashes?**

Done correctly, no. The lifting solution chemically reshapes the lashes' protein bonds — similar to how a chemical hair perm works, but milder and shorter contact. We use professional solutions and standard processing times. The risk of damage comes almost entirely from overprocessing (leaving solution on too long), which is why technique matters.

**Q: Lash lift vs. lash extensions — what's the difference?**

Lash lifts curl and lift your own natural lashes. Extensions add synthetic or natural-fiber lashes glued to your own. Lifts are lower maintenance (no infills, no special cleansers), last 6–8 weeks, and let you wear mascara normally. Extensions look more dramatic but require regular infills every 2–3 weeks and careful aftercare.

**Q: How long does brow lamination last?**

Usually 4–6 weeks. The brow hairs gradually return to their natural direction as they grow. Many clients combine brow lamination with brow tinting for a more complete and longer-visible result.

**Q: Can I wear mascara after a lash lift?**

Yes — wait 24–48 hours after the lift, then mascara as normal. Many clients find they actually use less mascara because the natural curl is already there.

**Q: Is brow lamination the same as microblading?**

No — they're very different. Microblading is a semi-permanent tattoo that creates the appearance of hair strokes in sparse brow areas (lasts 1–3 years). Brow lamination is a chemical treatment that smooths and lifts your existing brow hairs into a fluffy, defined shape (lasts 4–6 weeks). Lamination is much lower commitment and works best when you have brow hair to work with.

**Q: Are these services pregnancy-safe?**

Most providers recommend avoiding the chemical solutions used in lash lifts and brow lamination during pregnancy, particularly in the first trimester, out of an abundance of caution. Lash and brow tinting is generally fine but we'll talk through your specific situation. Always mention pregnancy when you book.

**Q: Can I combine lash and brow services with a facial?**

Yes — this is one of our most-booked combinations. Book a facial followed by lash & brow services in the same visit. Your esthetician will sequence the timing so nothing interferes (lash chemistry first, facial work second is the typical order). [Not sure which facial to pair?](which-facial-should-i-get.html)

**Q: How often should I redo these treatments?**

Lash lifts: every 6–8 weeks. Brow lamination: every 4–6 weeks. Tinting: every 3–6 weeks. Many regulars book a recurring combo every 5–6 weeks to stay continuously polished without thinking about it.

**Q: Will my lashes look weird if I don't continue?**

No. The lift grows out naturally as your lashes shed (the cycle is 6–8 weeks anyway). You won't be left with damaged or weird-looking lashes — just your natural ones, the same as before. Same with brow lamination.

# Smooth, Without the *Awkward*

## Waxing, Done the Way You'd Want

Waxing is one of those services where the technician matters more than the location, the price, or the brand. A skilled wax tech makes the experience feel quick, professional, and routine — even for Brazilians, even for first-timers. An unskilled one can make the same service feel rushed, painful, or just awkward in ways that take the experience from "something I do every six weeks" to "something I dread."

Our team takes waxing seriously. Calm, confident, no commentary. You're in and out efficiently without ever feeling rushed. We've trained on body areas across the full spectrum, we know how to keep conversation light when conversation is welcome and stay quiet when it isn't, and we'll never make you feel anything less than completely respected in the room.

### Why we list pricing publicly

You'll notice every service on our waxing menu shows its price. We do this because waxing is one of those services where opacity makes people anxious — "I'm about to pay how much for this?" is not the question we want you asking on the table. Prices are listed below. No surprises.

## What to Expect at Your Appointment

### Plan to arrive about 5 minutes early

We're by appointment only, so plan to arrive 5 minutes early. When it's time to come inside, we'll send you a text. You'll be greeted with your choice of soothing tea or cold water and walked back to a private treatment room.

### You'll change in private

Your technician will step out while you undress only as much as the area you're waxing requires. For brow, lip, and chin: you stay dressed. For underarm, arm, back, or leg: you'll partially undress with draping. For bikini or Brazilian: from the waist down, with full draping until the moment of the wax.

### The wax itself

Most body waxing is done with hard wax that's applied warm and removed without strips — gentler on skin and more thorough on coarse hair than older strip-wax techniques. Your technician will work in sections, applying and removing each in just a few seconds. Brazilian waxes typically take 25–35 minutes total; brow waxes are usually under 10.

### You'll leave with aftercare guidance

What to avoid for the next 24–48 hours (heat, tight clothing, exfoliating products), and how to set up a maintenance routine to minimize ingrowns and maximize how long results last.

## If This Is Your First Wax

Especially if it's your first Brazilian or bikini wax, here's what we want you to know:

### Hair length matters

About **1/4 inch** is the sweet spot — roughly two weeks of growth from a clean shave. Too short and the wax can't grip the hair. Too long and the process is more uncomfortable than it needs to be. If you're not sure if you're ready, text us a photo (clothed, of just the length you have grown out) and we'll tell you honestly.

### Don't shave between waxes

The single biggest mistake new wax clients make is "tidying up" with a razor between appointments. This resets the hair growth cycle and undoes the gradual thinning benefit that consistent waxing provides. If you wax, just wax. We promise it's easier in the long run.

### Caffeine and alcohol increase sensitivity

If you have the choice, skip your morning coffee and last night's wine before your appointment. Both can make skin more reactive to the wax.

### Ibuprofen 30 minutes before helps

Not required, but if you're nervous about discomfort, 400–600mg of ibuprofen taken 30 minutes before your wax can take the edge off meaningfully.

### It really does get easier

The first Brazilian is the hardest. The second is meaningfully easier. By the fifth, most regulars describe it as a quick, routine appointment they barely think about. Hair grows back finer and less densely each time.

### Tell your technician it's your first time

We'll go slower, explain what's happening, and check in throughout. We've done thousands of first waxes — nothing about your experience will surprise us.

## Aftercare

### First 24 hours

- No heat — skip hot showers, baths, saunas, and steam rooms.
- No exercise — sweat irritates freshly waxed skin.
- No sun exposure — freshly waxed skin is more sun-sensitive.
- No tight clothing in the area — loose is better for the first day.
- No exfoliation — physical or chemical, give it a day.
- No sexual activity for 24 hours after a Brazilian — the skin needs to settle.

### Ongoing care between waxes

- **Exfoliate gently** 2–3 times per week starting day 3 — a soft washcloth, KP Bump Eraser, or a gentle chemical exfoliant.
- **Moisturize daily** to keep the skin supple and prevent dryness from contributing to ingrowns.
- **Avoid heavy oils** right at the follicle openings — some lotions can clog and cause bumps.
- **Don't shave between waxes** — the most important rule.

### If you get an ingrown

Don't pick or dig. Apply warm compresses 2–3 times a day to soften the skin and encourage the hair to surface naturally. If you're prone to ingrowns, ask your technician for product recommendations — there are excellent over-the-counter options that prevent most cases.

## Common Combinations

Most of our regulars book one of these stacks:

### The "morning routine reduction" stack

Brazilian + underarm + brow + lip. About 60 minutes total. The full set of "things you'd otherwise be doing in front of a mirror," done in one calm visit every 4–6 weeks.

### The "pre-vacation" stack

Brazilian + bikini line cleanup + full leg + underarm. About 90 minutes total. The week before you leave for the beach. Don't forget the SPF for the freshly waxed skin.

### The pre-wedding stack

Book waxing 5–7 days before the wedding (not the day before — you want any redness fully settled by the day of). Pair with [lash lift, brow lamination, and tinting](lash-and-brow-chattanooga.html) for the complete pre-wedding prep.

### The maintenance combo

A single area (brow, lip, or underarm) every 4 weeks. The cheapest, simplest version of waxing maintenance — popular for clients who shave the rest themselves.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: How long does hair need to be for waxing?**

About 1/4 inch (roughly 2 weeks of growth from a clean shave). Too short and the wax can't grip; too long and the process is more uncomfortable than it needs to be. If you're between waxes and unsure, text us and we'll help you decide whether to schedule now or wait.

**Q: Does waxing hurt?**

There's discomfort, especially the first few times. It's brief — the actual hair removal is over in seconds per pull. Most clients describe the discomfort as a sharp pinch rather than a sustained pain. Pain decreases dramatically over time as the hair grows back finer and less densely. Many regulars say their fourth or fifth Brazilian feels half as intense as their first.

**Q: How often should I wax?**

Every 4–6 weeks is the standard cadence. The hair grows back on roughly that cycle, and consistent waxing trains the hair to grow back finer over time. Going longer between visits means more discomfort and less of the "hair-thinning" compounding benefit.

**Q: What about ingrown hairs?**

Ingrowns are the most common waxing complaint and are largely preventable. Exfoliate gently 2–3 times per week between waxes (a soft washcloth or KP Bump Eraser works well), avoid tight clothing immediately after a wax, and keep the area moisturized. We'll give you specific recommendations based on your skin and which area you're waxing.

**Q: Can I wax during my period?**

Yes, with a tampon in place. Be aware that skin tends to be more sensitive during the few days before and the first days of your period, so the wax may feel more intense. If you have flexibility, scheduling 7–10 days after your period starts is the sweet spot for comfort.

**Q: Will I need to undress completely?**

Only the area being waxed needs to be exposed. We provide draping and step out of the room when you change. For face waxing (brow, lip, chin), you stay fully clothed. For Brazilian, bikini, and leg waxing, you'll undress from the waist down with draping in place.

**Q: Is this my first wax — what do I need to know?**

Show up clean, with hair grown out to about 1/4 inch. Avoid caffeine and alcohol that day (they increase skin sensitivity). Take ibuprofen 30 minutes before if you're nervous about discomfort. Tell us it's your first time — we'll go slower, explain everything, and check in throughout.

**Q: Can I get waxed while pregnant?**

Yes, with one caveat: pregnancy increases skin sensitivity, so waxing may feel more intense than usual. Many clients still wax through their entire pregnancy. We'll check in throughout your appointment and adapt pressure and pacing accordingly.

**Q: What if I have to cancel last-minute?**

Same-day cancellations and no-shows are difficult on our small team. We have a cancellation policy in place — please give us as much notice as possible. If something genuinely unexpected comes up, just text us and we'll work it out.

**Q: Why is Brazilian and bikini for female clients only?**

This is a policy decision that reflects our team's training and comfort. Our wax technicians are trained and certified in techniques appropriate for our current client base. We respect every client who walks in our door and will gladly help refer you elsewhere if our menu doesn't fit your needs.

# Sound Bath Sessions

Chattanooga Sound Baths

# Lie Down. Let the *Bowls* Do the Work.

Immersive group and private sound baths in our North Chattanooga studio. Crystal singing bowls, gongs, and chimes — the most accessible meditative experience there is.

[See Upcoming Sessions](https://amberandsagespa.com/#event)

## What Actually Happens in a Sound Bath

You arrive at our studio, get settled on a mat with bolsters, blankets, and an eye pillow. Lights dim. Your sound practitioner welcomes you with a few words, sometimes a short reiki intention or a brief breath practice. Then the bowls begin.

Crystal singing bowls produce long, sustained tones tuned to specific frequencies. As the practitioner moves through the bowls, the overlapping vibrations create an acoustic environment that's almost impossible to think through — in the best way. Your nervous system downshifts. Most guests describe it as a kind of waking sleep, with occasional vivid imagery or surprising emotional release. A gong or two punctuate the session. You'll re-emerge slowly, gently, and usually a little disoriented in the best way possible.

### Who comes to our sound baths

Honestly, all kinds of people. Some are deep into meditation practice and find that sound bypasses the mental chatter they fight elsewhere. Some are skeptics dragged by a friend who become regulars by the end. Some are dealing with grief, postpartum overwhelm, burnout, or insomnia and find that 60 minutes here resets something that 20 hours of sleep can't.

- **First-time meditators** — sound does the work for you.
- **High-stress professionals** — nervous-system reset without effort.
- **People processing loss** — safe container, gentle release.
- **Postpartum and prenatal guests** — rest while still being held in a community space.
- **Athletes and runners** — recovery you can't get from foam rolling.
- **Anyone with insomnia or anxiety** — many regulars sleep deeply the night after a session.

### Group sessions are seasonal

Our group sound baths are held in our studio on a rotating monthly basis — new moon and seasonal events are favorites. Check our [events section](https://amberandsagespa.com/#event) for the next scheduled session, or follow us on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/amberandsagespa/) for announcements.

### Private and pairings

If group settings aren't your thing, we offer private sound therapy sessions in a treatment room. You can also pair a sound session with reiki for a deeper nervous-system experience, or end an Eminence facial or massage with a brief sound finisher. Inquire when you book or text us for custom pairings.

### What it feels like physically

Some guests feel the bowls in their chest, hands, or hips — literally a sensation of vibration. Others mostly feel an emotional softening. A few drift off entirely. There's no "right" way to experience a sound bath. We provide tissues for the emotional, blankets for the cold, and water for the dry-mouthed.

## How Sound Pairs With Our Other Services

### Sound + Reiki

The most popular combination. Reiki opens the energetic field; sound deepens it. A common 75-minute private session.

### Sound + Yin Yoga

Long-held yin postures with sound layered in. We schedule these as special group events — check the events section.

### Sound + Massage

Available as a custom enhancement after deep tissue, when the nervous system needs help integrating.

### New Moon Group Sessions

A seasonal favorite. We post the next date on our homepage promo banner.

[See Upcoming Events](https://amberandsagespa.com/#event)

## Sound Bath FAQ

**Q: What is a sound bath?**

A sound bath is a guided session in which you lie comfortably while a practitioner plays crystal singing bowls, gongs, chimes, and tuning forks. The overlapping tones produce a deeply meditative state — many guests describe a kind of waking sleep.

**Q: Do I have to know how to meditate?**

No. Sound baths are one of the easiest entry points to meditative states because the sound does most of the work — you don't have to manage your attention. First-time guests are welcome and common.

**Q: What should I wear and bring?**

Wear soft, warm layers. We provide mats, bolsters, blankets, and eye pillows, but you're welcome to bring your own if it helps you settle. Avoid heavy meals an hour beforehand.

**Q: How long is a session?**

Most group sound baths run 60 minutes, with a few minutes of arrival/settling and a few minutes of gentle re-emergence at the end. Private sessions can be customized for length.

**Q: Is a sound bath safe during pregnancy?**

Generally yes, though we recommend talking with your provider first. The volume is moderate and non-startling, and we offer side-lying positioning with extra cushions for comfort.

**Q: What if I cry, fall asleep, or have a strong reaction?**

All normal. Sound work can move stuck emotion, and many guests doze off. We hold space without judgment — you're free to experience whatever surfaces.

# Aura Photography

Aura Photography in Chattanooga

# See Your *Energy*

A 15-minute experience that produces a portrait you'll keep forever — captured with the **AuraCloud 3D Pro**, the most advanced aura imaging system available, here at Amber & Sage Spa.

[Book Your Aura Session](https://booking.mangomint.com/amberandsage?serviceId=112)
[How It Works](#how-it-works)

## The Most Unusual Thing on Our Menu

You can get a massage at a hundred places in Chattanooga. You can get a facial at most of them too. But the chance to sit down, place your hand on a biofeedback sensor, and take home an actual portrait of your energy field — that's something different. People come to Amber & Sage for this specifically, often on birthdays, after big life transitions, before weddings, or just because the idea is irresistible.

Some clients arrive curious. Some arrive skeptical. Almost everyone leaves with a printed photo they want to frame, a story they want to tell, and a deeper understanding of what they were carrying that day. # Buccal Facial Massage

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/best-buccal-massage-chattanooga.html

A Local Guide

# The Best Buccal Massage in *Chattanooga*

Buccal massage is a niche, advanced facial technique that very few Chattanooga estheticians offer. Here's what it is, why people seek it out, and how to find a qualified provider.

[Book a Facial with Buccal](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)
[Learn What It Is](#what-is)

A note: this guide is written by one of the few Chattanooga spas that offers buccal massage. We have an obvious bias. We're also one of the few places in the city you can actually book this treatment, so the alternatives are limited — we'll be honest about that too.

## What Buccal Massage Actually Is

Buccal massage — sometimes called "intra-oral facial massage" or just "the inside-the-cheek facial massage" — is a technique where your esthetician wears sterile gloves and works specific muscles of your jaw, cheeks, and lower face from *inside* the mouth as well as outside. It's been popular in European spa culture for decades and reached mainstream awareness in the US in the late 2010s.

The technique targets the muscles of mastication: masseter, medial and lateral pterygoid, buccinator. These are the muscles you chew, clench, and grind with — and they hold an enormous amount of tension that can't be effectively reached from the outside of the face alone. Releasing them produces three notable effects:

- **Jaw tension release** — especially helpful for clenchers, grinders, and anyone with mild TMJ tightness.
- **Lymphatic drainage** — the buccal area drains lymph from the lower face; releasing it visibly reduces puffiness.
- **Structural lift** — the lower face looks visibly more defined and lifted afterward, with effects lasting days to weeks.

## What to Look for in a Chattanooga Buccal Provider

### 1. Specific training, not just licensure

Buccal massage is not part of standard esthetics curriculum in Tennessee. It's a post-licensure technique that estheticians learn through specialized continuing education — often through brand certifications (Eminence, Biologique Recherche), masterclasses, or international training. Ask your provider where she learned and whether buccal is something she does regularly or as a one-off.

### 2. Sterile gloves and proper hygiene

This is non-negotiable. Your esthetician should be visibly wearing fresh disposable gloves (typically nitrile), and you should be offered a brief rinse before and after. Ask if you're unsure.

### 3. Real consultation about your jaw

A good buccal provider will ask about TMJ history, recent dental work, oral health, and clenching/grinding habits before she starts. If she doesn't ask, that's a flag — certain TMJ conditions, recent dental surgery, or active oral infections are contraindications.

### 4. As part of a larger facial, not a standalone

The best buccal experiences happen inside a full facial, where lymphatic drainage and product application complement the work. Standalone "buccal-only" treatments exist but are usually less effective than buccal-as-part-of-a-90-minute-facial.

### 5. Realistic expectations

A good provider will tell you what to expect: noticeable lift for several days, some soreness in the jaw the next day (especially the first time), and best results when done in a series. If you're being promised "permanent" results, find someone else.

### Who really benefits

Clenchers, grinders, anyone with chronic jaw tension, anyone who notices puffiness in the lower face after travel or poor sleep, and anyone with a wedding or event coming up. Less impactful (though still pleasant) for people without significant jaw tension to begin with.

## How We Approach Buccal Massage

### A standalone 2-hour service, not an add-on

Our **Buccal Facial Massage is its own dedicated 2-hour service**, not an enhancement layered onto a regular facial. We made that choice intentionally: doing buccal properly — warming the muscles, doing thorough intra-oral work on both sides, holding pressure long enough to actually release, and integrating with a full facial flow — takes time. Trying to squeeze it onto the end of a 60-minute facial shortchanges the work. The 2-hour session is the right container.

### Trained, certified estheticians

Our estheticians have completed specific buccal training and perform the technique regularly. Tell us when you book and we'll match you with the right provider on the schedule.

### Hygiene protocol

Sterile nitrile gloves, fresh for every guest. Optional rinse before and after. Disposable everything that touches the inside of your mouth.

### Consultation that actually screens

Before the first buccal session, we'll ask about TMJ history, recent dental work, oral surgery, and what you're hoping to address. If buccal isn't a fit, we'll tell you and recommend something else (often facial cupping or aggressive lymphatic massage).

### What to expect afterward

Most clients feel mild soreness in the jaw the next day, similar to having done a hard chewing workout. Lift and reduced puffiness are typically visible immediately and last several days. Repeated sessions amplify and extend the effect.

## Where Else You Might Find Buccal Massage in Chattanooga

Buccal is genuinely rare in this market — in Chattanooga and the surrounding region, it's offered at only a small number of spas. If we don't have availability that works for you, here's how to vet alternatives:

- **Med-spas** — some include intra-oral massage as part of "facial lifting" packages. Quality varies; ask about specific training.
- **Aesthetic dentistry offices** — rarely, dental hygienists trained in TMJ release will offer therapeutic intra-oral work. Different goal than a facial, but related technique.
- **Independent estheticians** — a few in the broader region have done European training and offer buccal in their private studios. Worth searching for if availability matters more than convenience.
- **Atlanta and Nashville** — for buccal as a destination experience, both cities have more options. A road trip can be worth it for a special occasion.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is buccal massage?**

Buccal massage is an intra-oral facial massage technique. The esthetician wears gloves and works specific muscles of the jaw, cheeks, and lower face from inside the mouth as well as outside. It releases jaw tension, supports lymphatic flow, and creates a noticeable lift in the lower face.

**Q: Does buccal massage hurt?**

It's surprisingly intense — particularly if you carry tension in your jaw — but should never be sharply painful. Many guests describe it as feeling "deeply needed" even when the pressure is significant. Communicate with your esthetician throughout.

**Q: How is buccal massage different from a regular facial massage?**

Traditional facial massage works only the external skin and surface muscles. Buccal massage reaches the muscles of mastication (the muscles you chew with) — masseter, pterygoid, buccinator — which can't be effectively released from the outside alone. The lift you see afterward is structural, not just temporary.

**Q: Is buccal massage safe?**

Yes, when performed by a trained, licensed esthetician using sterile gloves. It's contraindicated for active oral infections, recent dental surgery, or certain TMJ conditions — your esthetician will screen for these in the consultation.

**Q: How often should I get buccal massage?**

For maintenance, once a month is plenty. For a noticeable cumulative effect (event prep, post-illness recovery), a series of three to five weekly sessions is more impactful.

**Q: Will I be sore after?**

Often, yes — especially after the first session and especially if you're a clencher. Soreness feels similar to having chewed gum for too long and resolves in 24–48 hours.

# What is Buccal Massage?

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/what-is-buccal-massage.html

Educational Guide

# What is *Buccal Massage?*

The European facial technique that reaches the muscles of your jaw from *inside* your mouth — explained without the hype.

[Book a Facial with Buccal](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)
[How It Works](#how-it-works)

## The Short Answer

Buccal massage — sometimes called "intra-oral facial massage" — is a specialized facial technique in which a trained, gloved esthetician works the muscles of the jaw, cheeks, and lower face from inside the mouth. The name comes from "buccal," the Latin-derived anatomical term for cheek. The technique has roots in European spa traditions and reached widespread Western attention through high-end European facialists like Anastasia Achilleos in the early 2010s.

The treatment usually adds 10–20 minutes to a facial. The esthetician wears sterile gloves and works one cheek at a time, using a combination of inside-the-mouth and outside-the-face pressure to release the buccinator, masseter, and pterygoid muscles. The effect: visible lift in the lower face, reduced puffiness, and meaningful release of jaw tension.

## The Anatomy It's Actually Working On

Your lower face contains several powerful muscles that traditional facial massage can only partly reach:

- **Masseter** — the main chewing muscle, running from your cheekbone down to your jaw. Holds enormous tension in clenchers and grinders. Felt clearly when you bite down.
- **Buccinator** — flat muscle in the cheek wall, between the inner cheek and the outer skin. Used in chewing, smiling, and forming sounds. Often tight in people who hold tension in the face.
- **Medial and lateral pterygoid** — deep jaw muscles that control side-to-side movement. Heavily implicated in TMJ symptoms.
- **Orbicularis oris and surrounding muscles** — the ring of muscle around the mouth.

From outside the face, you can press against the masseter and feel something happen. But you can't reach the buccinator, you can't access the pterygoids, and you can't apply the sustained pinching pressure that releases adhesions inside the cheek wall. Buccal massage reaches all of these. The lift you see afterward is mechanical — you've released held tension in muscles that were pulling the lower face down and forward.

## What It Helps With

### Jaw tension and mild TMJ symptoms

The most common reason people seek out buccal. Clenching and grinding produce chronic tightness in the masseter and pterygoids. Buccal massage releases this directly — in many cases, more effectively than night guards alone (which mitigate damage but don't release tension).

### Lower face lifting and contouring

When the buccinator, masseter, and surrounding muscles are tight, they pull the lower face down and forward. Releasing them allows the face to settle into its natural lifted position. Effects are visible immediately and last days to weeks.

### Lymphatic drainage

The buccal area is rich in lymphatic vessels. Working it directly supports drainage of stagnant lymph, which reduces visible puffiness — particularly noticeable in the lower face after travel, poor sleep, or alcohol.

### Headache relief

Many tension headaches involve referred pain from chronic jaw muscle tightness. Releasing the masseter and pterygoids can reduce both frequency and intensity for people prone to tension headaches.

### Facial expression and animation

People often report subtle improvements in how their face moves — smoother smiling, more natural facial animation — after a series of buccal treatments. This makes sense anatomically: muscles released from chronic gripping have more range of motion.

### What it is *not*

Buccal massage is not a substitute for medical TMJ treatment, a replacement for dental work, or a "filler alternative" in the sense of producing volume. It releases tension and lifts what's already there — it doesn't add volume.

## Who Benefits Most

- **Clenchers and grinders** — the most dramatic improvements happen here.
- **People with chronic jaw tension or mild TMJ** — not as a medical treatment, but as supportive care.
- **Anyone with persistent lower-face puffiness** — particularly under the jawline.
- **Mature skin** — the lifting effect addresses age-related downward pull effectively.
- **Pre-event prep** — weddings, photoshoots, big moments.
- **Tension-headache sufferers** — worth trying as part of a broader approach.

## What a Session Actually Looks Like

Buccal is typically performed as part of a longer facial. After cleansing, exfoliation, and possibly extractions, the esthetician puts on fresh nitrile gloves. She'll offer you a brief rinse with mouthwash if you'd like one. The buccal work then begins, usually starting with the outside of the masseter (warming up the area) before moving inside.

Inside-the-mouth work involves gentle pinching, sustained pressure, and slow gliding strokes across the buccinator and along the masseter. Some practitioners work the pterygoids by reaching back along the upper teeth. The pressure is firm but never sharp.

You'll likely feel a release at certain points — sometimes accompanied by emotional reactions (tears, laughter, sighs) since the jaw holds a lot of stored stress. This is normal and welcomed. The work continues on the other side. Total intra-oral time is usually 10–20 minutes.

Afterward, your esthetician will finish the facial with lymphatic drainage, mask, serums, and SPF. You'll leave with a noticeably lifted lower face and, often, mild soreness over the next day or two (similar to the day after chewing too much gum).

### Hygiene

Sterile single-use nitrile gloves. Fresh tools for every guest. Optional mouthwash rinse before and after.

### Screening

Before your first buccal session, we'll ask about TMJ history, recent dental work, oral surgery, current medications, and oral health. If buccal isn't right for you that day, we'll recommend something else.

### Integrated into the facial

Buccal works best inside a longer facial. The cleansing, mask, and lymphatic work before and after amplify the buccal benefits.

[Book a Facial with Buccal](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Where does the word "buccal" come from?**

Buccal comes from the Latin "bucca," meaning cheek. Anatomically, "buccal" refers to the area of the mouth that includes the inner cheek lining and the muscles of the cheek (especially the buccinator).

**Q: Is buccal massage the same as "face yoga" or "gua sha"?**

No. Face yoga uses facial exercises; gua sha uses a stone tool on the outside of the face. Buccal massage specifically reaches the muscles of mastication from inside the mouth — something neither face yoga nor gua sha can do effectively.

**Q: How long do the effects last?**

Visible lift and reduced puffiness typically last 3–7 days after a single session. With a series of weekly treatments, cumulative effects compound and last longer. For maintenance, monthly sessions work well.

**Q: Can I do buccal massage on myself?**

Lightly, yes — clean hands, gentle pressure, working masseter from inside the cheek. But you can't reach all the muscles effectively, and you can't apply the precise, sustained pressure a trained esthetician can. Self-massage is a fine maintenance tool between professional sessions.

**Q: Are there contraindications?**

Yes. Avoid buccal massage with active oral infections, recent oral surgery (within 4–6 weeks), recent dental work, certain TMJ conditions, or if you're on blood thinners. Pregnancy is generally fine but mention it during consultation.

**Q: What does it feel like emotionally?**

Many people experience emotional release during buccal work. The jaw holds a lot of stored stress, and releasing it can bring up tears or sighs unexpectedly. This is normal — your esthetician has seen it many times and will hold space without making it weird.

# What is Dermaplaning?

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/what-is-dermaplaning.html

Educational Guide

# What is *Dermaplaning?*

A clear explanation of dermaplaning — what it actually does, what it doesn't, and how it differs from the TikTok eyebrow-razor version.

[Book Dermaplaning](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)
[How It Works](#how-it-works)

## The Short Answer

Dermaplaning is a professional exfoliation treatment in which a licensed esthetician uses a sterile, surgical-grade scalpel held at a precise angle to gently remove the topmost layer of dead skin cells and the fine "peach fuzz" (vellus hair) from the face. It takes about 20–30 minutes when done as a standalone treatment, and is often added to a facial for combined benefit.

The instant result: dramatically smoother skin, brighter appearance, better product penetration, and noticeably better makeup application. The cumulative result, when done monthly: more even tone and reduced surface texture over time.

## How It Actually Works

Your skin renews itself on roughly a 28-day cycle — new skin cells form in the lower layers, migrate upward, and slough off when they reach the surface. As we age, this process slows down. Dead cells accumulate. Skin looks duller, feels rougher, and reflects light less evenly.

Dermaplaning manually removes that accumulated layer (called the stratum corneum). The scalpel is held at a shallow angle — about 45 degrees — and drawn across taut skin in short, light strokes. Done correctly, you feel almost nothing. Done incorrectly, you can get nicks or uneven results — which is why this is not a treatment to try yourself with a Tinkle blade and a YouTube tutorial.

The peach fuzz removal is a bonus. Vellus hair traps oil, dust, and product residue. Removing it makes skin look cleaner and lets serums penetrate without being filtered through hair first.

## Who Dermaplaning Is For

- **Anyone bothered by peach fuzz** — particularly visible in certain lights or under makeup.
- **People with dull, dry, or rough surface texture** — the immediate brightening is striking.
- **Anyone preparing for an event** — weddings, photoshoots, big presentations. Schedule 2–5 days before for optimal smoothness.
- **Mature skin** — cell turnover slows with age; dermaplaning compensates beautifully.
- **People who use a lot of skincare** — serums and treatments penetrate better through freshly exfoliated skin.

## Who It's Not For

- **Active acne** — dermaplaning can spread bacteria across pustular acne. Wait until the breakout clears.
- **Active rosacea flares** — can aggravate. Treat the underlying inflammation first.
- **Eczema on the face** — especially in active patches.
- **Recent Accutane use** — wait at least six months after stopping.
- **Cold sores or active oral herpes outbreaks** — postpone until cleared.
- **Pregnancy isn't a contraindication** — dermaplaning is non-chemical and pregnancy-safe.

### The "hair will grow back thicker" myth

No. Vellus hair (peach fuzz) is hormonally distinct from terminal hair (the kind on your scalp, eyebrows, and in beards). It doesn't have the follicular structure to grow in thicker. The hair returns at the same fineness and color it had before. The myth persists because terminal hair on the legs feels stubbly when it grows back — vellus hair simply doesn't.

## Professional vs. At-Home Tools

The at-home "dermaplaning" tools sold at Sephora and on Amazon are essentially eyebrow razors. They remove some peach fuzz on the very surface, which is fine. What they don't do — and can't do safely — is exfoliate the stratum corneum.

Professional dermaplaning uses a flexible, surgical-grade scalpel (typically a 10R blade) held by a trained esthetician at a precise angle. The result is dramatically deeper exfoliation done safely. At-home tools are fine for between-session maintenance; they are not a substitute for the real treatment.

## What to Expect at Your Appointment

A typical dermaplaning treatment goes like this: cleansing, sometimes a brief steam to soften skin, drying, then the dermaplaning itself in sections (forehead, cheeks, jaw, upper lip, neck). The esthetician pulls the skin taut with one hand and works the scalpel with the other. You'll hear a soft scraping sound — that's normal and means it's working. The treatment is comfortable; many clients say it feels like being lightly tickled. Afterward, your esthetician applies serums, a mask, and SPF.

The whole thing takes 20–30 minutes as a standalone, longer if combined with a facial (recommended — the dermaplaning maximizes the absorption of all the other steps).

## Dermaplaning at Amber & Sage

We offer dermaplaning as a standalone treatment or, more commonly, as an enhancement to our 60- or 90-minute [Eminence organic facials](eminence-organic-facials-chattanooga.html). The combination is hard to beat: dermaplaning first, then product layering with your skin at its most receptive.

### Trained estheticians

All of our estheticians are Tennessee-licensed and have completed advanced dermaplaning training. We're meticulous about sterile single-use blades, sanitation, and proper technique.

### Customized to your skin

We'll assess your skin before recommending dermaplaning. If something else would serve you better that visit (a peel, an extraction-focused session, a more hydrating protocol), we'll tell you.

### Aftercare guidance

You'll leave with simple instructions: SPF religiously for the next several days, no exfoliating acids or retinol for 48 hours, no aggressive skincare for a week. We'll send you home with the right products to support the result if you want them.

[Book Dermaplaning](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=9)

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Does dermaplaning make hair grow back thicker?**

No. This is one of the most persistent myths in skincare. Vellus hair (peach fuzz) grows back with the same diameter and same color it had before. The hair on your face doesn't have the hormonal triggers that produce thicker hair growth — that's why we don't shave our faces and develop beards.

**Q: How is professional dermaplaning different from at-home dermaplaning tools?**

At-home tools are essentially eyebrow razors and only remove surface peach fuzz. Professional dermaplaning uses a surgical-grade scalpel held at a precise angle by a trained esthetician. It removes peach fuzz AND a layer of dead skin cells (the stratum corneum), producing dramatically smoother results.

**Q: Is dermaplaning safe for sensitive skin?**

Usually yes. Dermaplaning is non-chemical and works on the surface only. It's contraindicated for active acne, rosacea flares, eczema on the treatment area, and certain medications (Accutane, blood thinners). Your esthetician will screen for these in consultation.

**Q: How long do dermaplaning results last?**

Peach fuzz typically grows back fully within 2–4 weeks. The exfoliation effect lasts about 3 weeks (one skin cycle). Most people who incorporate dermaplaning into their routine get it monthly.

**Q: Can I combine dermaplaning with an enzyme peel?**

Yes, and many people do — in the same session. Dermaplaning first removes dead surface skin, allowing the enzyme peel to work more evenly. Your esthetician will choose the right enzyme blend for your skin that day. [Curious how enzyme peels compare to chemical peels?](enzyme-peel-vs-chemical-peel.html)

**Q: How soon before an event should I schedule?**

2–5 days before is ideal. Skin will look its best within that window. Avoid scheduling the day of, because skin can be briefly more reactive immediately after.

# What is Cupping Therapy?

Source: https://amberandsagespa.com/what-is-cupping-therapy.html

Educational Guide

# What is *Cupping Therapy?*

The 3,000-year-old practice that made headlines on Michael Phelps' back — explained without the mystique.

[Book Cupping](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=21)
[How It Works](#how-it-works)

## The Short Answer

Cupping therapy is a manual treatment in which glass, silicone, or plastic cups are placed on the skin and a vacuum is created — either by heating the air inside (traditional fire cupping) or by mechanical suction (modern cupping). The cups stick to the skin, drawing tissue upward into the cup. The practitioner either leaves the cups stationary on key points or slides them along the body in a kind of inverse massage.

The practice originated in ancient Chinese and Egyptian medicine and has been used continuously for over 3,000 years. It re-entered Western mainstream awareness in 2016, when photographers caught Olympic swimmer Michael Phelps with the characteristic round marks on his back — suddenly everyone wanted to know what they were.

## What's Actually Happening

The traditional explanation: cupping moves stagnant energy ("qi") and blood, allowing the body's natural healing processes to resume. The modern physiological explanation: the suction pulls fascia away from the muscle layers underneath, decompressing tight tissue. This is the opposite of regular massage — instead of pressing tissue down, cupping pulls tissue up.

What the body experiences:

- **Fascial decompression** — tight, restricted fascia is pulled away from underlying structures, restoring slide and glide between tissue layers.
- **Increased local blood flow** — suction draws fresh blood into the area. This is what creates the marks — not bruising, but stagnant blood being pulled to the surface where the body can process it.
- **Lymphatic stimulation** — the negative pressure mobilizes lymph in the cupped area, supporting detoxification.
- **Parasympathetic activation** — like many sustained bodywork techniques, cupping calms the nervous system.

## About the Marks

The famous round cupping marks are the source of more confusion than anything else about the practice. Three things to know:

**They're not bruises.** A bruise is caused by blunt impact rupturing capillaries from outside. Cupping marks are caused by suction drawing stagnant blood and metabolic waste to the surface from inside. They look similar but feel completely different. Bruises hurt to touch; cupping marks generally don't.

**The color tells you something.** A practitioner trained in traditional cupping reads the color. Light pink marks indicate minimal stagnation. Dark purple or near-black marks indicate significant stagnation in that area — chronic tightness, restricted blood flow, or old injury patterns. Subsequent sessions in the same areas typically produce lighter marks as the tissue improves.

**They fade in 4–10 days.** Most marks meaningfully fade within a week. Lighter marks may resolve in 2–3 days. If you have an event where you'll show the cupped area, schedule cupping 7–10 days in advance to be safe.

### Cupping is not the same as a cupping massage gimmick

"Cupping facials" using tiny silicone cups for lymphatic drainage on the face are a related but much lighter technique. Therapeutic body cupping — the kind that addresses chronic tightness and produces visible marks — uses larger, stronger cups and requires real training.

## What Cupping Helps With

- **Chronic muscle tension** — especially in the back, shoulders, and neck. Cupping reaches restrictions that even deep tissue can struggle with.
- **Athletic recovery** — why it's so popular with elite athletes. Cupping accelerates the clearance of metabolic waste from heavily worked muscles.
- **Fascial adhesions** — old injuries, surgical scars, postural patterns that have created stuck fascia. Cupping decompresses these.
- **Respiratory issues** — in traditional medicine, cupping is used for congestion and breathing difficulties. Cupping over the upper back can help with stuck mucus.
- **IT band tightness** — runners and cyclists especially. Sliding cups along the IT band can produce noticeable improvement.
- **Stress and nervous-system overload** — the parasympathetic effect is significant.

## Types of Cupping

You may encounter several variations:

- **Stationary (or "fixed") cupping** — cups placed on specific points and left for 5–20 minutes. Produces the strongest marks.
- **Sliding (or "moving") cupping** — oil applied to the skin, cups slid across the body. Feels like a deep, inverse massage. Produces lighter, more diffuse marks.
- **Flash cupping** — quick repeated suction and release, used to stimulate blood flow without leaving marks.
- **Facial cupping** — small silicone cups for lymphatic drainage on the face. Gentle. No marks.
- **Fire cupping** — traditional method using a flame to heat air inside glass cups. Visually dramatic, equally effective.
- **Wet cupping** — involves controlled superficial incisions. Traditional medical practice; not typically offered at American spas.

## What to Expect at a Session

A cupping session typically lasts 30–60 minutes and is often combined with massage. Your practitioner will discuss your goals, identify areas of tightness, and clean the skin in the treatment area. She'll apply oil (for sliding cupping) and place the cups. You'll feel the suction immediately — a strong pulling sensation that should feel intense but pleasant.

Cups stay in place or slide along your back, shoulders, glutes, hamstrings, IT bands, or wherever you're being treated. After the work is complete, the cups are removed (with a gentle pressure release on the cup edge) and the marks become visible. Your practitioner will give aftercare instructions: hydrate generously, avoid intense exercise for 24 hours, keep the cupped areas warm, and skip alcohol that evening.

## Cupping at Amber & Sage

We offer cupping as a standalone treatment and as an enhancement to therapeutic massage. Our therapists are trained in modern silicone and glass cupping, with experience in sliding, stationary, and combined techniques.

### Combined with massage

The most popular configuration. We typically combine cupping with [deep tissue massage](deep-tissue-massage-chattanooga.html) — the cupping decompresses tight fascia, then the manual work addresses what's underneath. Often more effective than either alone.

### For specific conditions

Common reasons clients book cupping with us: chronic upper back tension, IT band tightness for runners and cyclists, shoulder restriction, lower back stiffness, and post-event athletic recovery.

### What we screen for

Cupping isn't right for everyone. Contraindications include open wounds, severe varicose veins, active skin conditions in the treatment area, recent surgery, certain blood-thinning medications, and pregnancy abdomen/back. We'll ask before we start.

[Book Cupping](https://booking.mangomint.com/101649?showOnlyScId=21)

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Are the cupping marks bruises?**

Not technically. Bruises come from blunt impact that ruptures blood vessels. Cupping marks come from suction drawing stagnant blood and fluid into the surface of the skin. They don't hurt the way bruises do, and they fade in 4–10 days. The color and intensity reflect the level of stagnation in that area.

**Q: Does cupping hurt?**

Most people describe it as a strong, satisfying pulling sensation — the opposite of pressure. Sliding cupping (moving the cups along the body) feels like an unusual but pleasant massage. The intensity is controllable and your practitioner will adjust.

**Q: What's the difference between dry cupping and wet cupping?**

Dry cupping (what most spas offer, including ours) uses suction only. Wet cupping involves making small superficial incisions to draw out a small amount of blood — this is a traditional medical practice and is not performed at most American spas. If you see "cupping" on a spa menu, assume dry cupping unless specified otherwise.

**Q: Should I hide the marks if I have an event?**

Schedule cupping 7–10 days before any event where you'll show your back, shoulders, or wherever the cups were placed. Most marks fade meaningfully within a week. If you're getting cupping for the first time, do it on an area you can cover for at least a week.

**Q: How often can I get cupping?**

For chronic conditions, weekly for a few weeks then taper to monthly is typical. For athletic recovery, immediately after hard training is common. For maintenance, monthly works well.

**Q: Any aftercare I should know about?**

Hydrate generously. Avoid intense exercise, alcohol, and very hot showers for 24 hours. Keep cupped areas covered and warm. The body is processing the released waste; support it with water and rest.
